title: The server: what it loads and asks per request
grade_reasons: 559 of 562 pages, 181 of 268 route handlers and the proxy each load the same 10 to 12 MB of server code whatever their job: 0.84 to 1.3 s and 71 to 97 MB to start cold on the review machine, against 0.16 to 0.24 s and 14 to 26 MB for the health check. A product view asks the database about 18 times where one answer changes per view, every store page load makes one or two more function calls for nothing, and each admin shell render spends 125 ms building its menu. Nothing on the server side holds any of it (the one server budget, the first byte of two warm pages, cannot see these costs), which is the letter of a D. It is not an E: nothing hurts a person or costs real money before opening, and the caching design is sound (82 of 85 cached reads tagged, a warm cached page asks nothing of its own, the docs are static). The second reviewers' numbers confirm the first draft's D. The ladder counts the findings' work items only: they end at a strong B, and the A needs the three gap items and the owner's yes on store domains.

measures.name: Server code a cold function loads, by kind of entry
measures.today: By next analyze on the review's build: /api/visit 1,890 modules and 10,475 KB; /s/[store]/[market] 2,419 and 11,944 KB; /admin/[store]/orders 2,349 and 12,068 KB; the proxy 18 chunks and 9,729 KB (1,309 to 1,311 source files); /api/health 308 and 1,155 KB. One import cycle of 229 files in src/server is reached by 559 of 562 pages, 181 of 268 handlers and the proxy. 24 public handlers of 7 to 52 lines each load all of it. Cold load in a fresh process: 0.84 to 1.3 s for a fat entry, 0.16 to 0.24 s for /api/health. Source: digest/server-graph.md, digest/functions.md, m/chunks.md.
measures.target_a: A beacon (the four /api/visit routes, /api/recommendations/events): 1.0 MB and 500 modules or fewer, and a cold load within 100 ms of /api/health's on the same machine. The proxy: 1.2 MB of chunks and 120 source files or fewer, reaching none of auth.ts, pages.ts, catalog.ts, stores.ts, admin-text.ts or sharp. A storefront page: 4.0 MB and 1,500 modules or fewer, with no admin text, AI tools, theme-store code or sharp, and no Stripe SDK off the pay routes. An admin list page: 6.5 MB or fewer, with only the text areas it draws and no AI engine before the assistant is opened. The largest import cycle in src/server: 19 files or fewer. Every handler over 1,500 modules is on a named list with its reason (181 today; about 29 expected).
measures.how_measured: src/server/route-load.graph.test.ts with src/server/route-load.baseline.json on every pnpm test (source files reached per entry, forbidden modules, the largest cycle), and scripts/route-budget.mjs after pnpm build in CI's e2e job (the chunks each built entry names; today plus 4%, may only fall). Both are made by the guard item. The module and KB figures come from docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/server-graph.mjs over a next analyze export.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floors are measured. /api/health loads about 0.4 MB once the unused schema is out; Next's own runtime is about 544 modules and 0.5 MB on a page; the simulated end of every planned cut is 0.96 MB for the beacon, 0.8 MB for the proxy, 3.5 MB for a storefront page and about 6 MB for an admin page. The targets sit 4 to 50% above those floors, because the simulation removes whole edges and a real change keeps small parts. A B stops when the cycle is cut: beacon 1.9 MB, proxy 2.4 MB, admin 8.2 MB. Knowingly left in: all four storefront languages (0.4 MB) and every block's server component in the page renderer, because one function serves every store.

measures.name: What every instance pays before its first request
measures.today: Start hook: 856 modules, 2,383 KB of chunks, 0.27 to 0.34 s and 26 to 43 MB before the first request of every function, lean ones included (383 source files; the reader alone needs about 50). Then one query, and one a minute per instance (278,393 runs in 78 days on an empty table). Server-reference manifest: 10,397,955 bytes and 81,027 route entries; 80 to 91 ms and 20 to 24 MB to read, parse and freeze. The unused Drizzle schema: 56 to 114 ms and about 7 MB per copy, in 6 built files. All from the review machine. Nothing times a cold start in production. Source: digest/server-graph.md, digest/functions.md.
measures.target_a: Start hook: 60 source files or fewer by static imports and under 0.7 MB of chunks, with no ai.ts, auth.ts or admin text. Schema: 0 built files hold table definitions. Manifest: under 5 MB and 40,000 entries, or a production reading that shows its load under 30 ms per cold start. A production figure exists and has a target: cold starts a day, and their p50 and p95 time to the first answer by kind of entry.
measures.how_measured: The graph test's baseline for src/instrumentation.ts. scripts/route-budget.mjs prints the hook's chunk bytes and the manifest's bytes and entry count on every CI build; each may only fall. rg -l -F '.table("theme_schedules"' .next/server -g '*.js' prints nothing. In production: the instance.start log line proposed in the third gap.
measures.why_this_is_a: Every function pays these, the health check included, so they set the floor of every cold start: about 0.45 s of a lean route's 0.6 s today. The hook's floor is the database client and the reader (47 to 52 files). The manifest's floor is not known: Next keeps one list for all routes, and the planned cuts take it only to about 9.4 MB. That is a B. An A needs it halved, or shown cheap where it really runs.

measures.name: Database statements per storefront view, warm
measures.today: An anonymous view of a prerendered product: about 18, 16 beyond the proxy's; stock is the one answer that changes per view and is read twice. Search 11 to 12, with search_rules read twice. Category about 2. Home and a store's own page 0 of their own. A shopper with a cart: 2 identical cart counts per page. A signed-in shopper on a product page: 2 to 4 session reads. A cart with lines and the checkout were never counted. Source: digest/storefront-data.md (pg_stat_database before and after one GET on the local production build).
measures.target_a: Product page: 3 or fewer beyond the proxy's, all on the inventory tables (4 for a store with producer schemes or price breaks). Category 2. Search 10 or fewer and no settings table read twice. Home and built pages 0. One cart count and one session read per request. A cart with three lines and the checkout: counted, read in at most two waves after the shopper is known, and under a budget.
measures.how_measured: scripts/server-budget.mjs in CI's e2e job, made by the storefront budget item: xact_commit and the table counters before and after one GET of each page, failing above a kept budget. The same counter as the admin's (AD-12) serves the integration tests.
measures.why_this_is_a: Stock is the one catalogue fact read per request by written rule (docs/rules/storefront.md), so the floor of a product view is one read. Everything else on the page changes only when an owner saves, and belongs in the prerendered page. 3 allows stock, one read for a store with schemes or breaks, and one for the minute poll's noise. A B is the 15 that sharing reads within one request gives. One read stays in front of every page by design: the proxy's store facts, once per store, instance and 10 seconds, which is what makes a private store private within seconds.

measures.name: Function runs a store page view causes beyond its document
measures.today: /wishlist/saved on 12 of 12 store pages measured (twice on checkout), each also a proxy run. /api/shop/tiles with 3 statements on every page with a product grid, though both tile switches default to off. A render function on every view of 148 of 149 prerendered store routes: 97,919 of the demo home's 138,523 bytes are streamed per view to place two cart badges and a country hint. One Add to cart: 16 requests and 193 KB. 13 to 44 requests per page load pass the proxy, 18 of the cart page's 42 prefetches for pages a press cannot open. Crawlers on Next's bot list get a full render even of the 508 static pages. Source: m/routes.json, digest/caching.md.
measures.target_a: For a visitor with no cart, wishlist or account, on a store with tile stock off: 0 function calls after the document. Home, built, blog and info pages are 'static' in the prerender manifest and answer as cache hits (21 of the demo's 148 resuming routes). Product, listing, cart, checkout and account pages keep their one per-request part. One Add to cart: 1 request under 5 KB. A Bingbot request for a static page is a cache HIT. No prefetch through the proxy for a page a press cannot open.
measures.how_measured: scripts/render-modes.mjs with scripts/render-modes.baseline.json after the build in CI (compute mode and holes per route; made by CA-16's item). Request counts after load and after one Add to cart in e2e/performance.spec.ts. docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs for the 12 store pages.
measures.why_this_is_a: The floor is zero: Kaizena Flow's docs already answer with no function, and what differs per visitor on a home page is two badges and a hint. Product and listing pages keep a per-request part because stock and filters are per request by rule. That is the stated tolerance, with /themes, which keeps a function per view so its filter works without scripts. The proxy still runs once per page request: it carries each store's address rules and cannot go. A B stops at removing the wishlist and tile calls.

measures.name: Statements before an admin screen shows its first content
measures.today: Store Home: 29 to 46 statements before its first content, plus 2 for the guard, one of them thrown away. Store shell on a hard load: 6 statements, 5 in a row, 2 more after every render, and one Supabase Auth call per request for a session without two-step. Products list: 16 or more for an editor, 12 unused. Orders list 9 to 11. Platform Home 18 plus 6 or 7 in the layout. Payments 9 in 5 waves. Five lists read everything: products, customers (after grouping every order), the platform's stores, pages and articles (two whole documents per page, 0.64 ms each). Source: digest/admin-data.md.
measures.target_a: Store Home: first content after 14 statements or fewer in at most 2 waves. Shell: 2 for the guard plus one wave, 0 after the response once a store's test account is known active, 0 Auth calls for an account with no factor. Products list 5 or fewer. Orders list 2 fewer than today. Platform Home 11 or fewer. Payments 7 or fewer in 2 waves. Every list reads one page of rows and no page document.
measures.how_measured: src/server/admin-statements.int.test.ts with src/server/admin-statements.baseline.json (five screens; a count may only fall) and, in production, the admin.render log line with a statements count per render. Both are made by AD-12's item.
measures.why_this_is_a: The guard's two reads are a security decision and stay per request. A home that shows eight figures needs about one statement per family of figures: 14 in two waves is what folding the count-only reads reaches with each figure's permission rule kept, and a pool of 5 connections runs them in three rounds. A B is the 22 the small steps give. Lists must be bounded before real catalogues exist: an unbounded read is free on 10 demo products and is the first thing to hurt at 2,000.

measures.name: What one save, poll or redraw costs in the admin
measures.today: Menu build: 125 ms of blocking CPU per store shell render (220 permission lookups for 110 paths; 243 ms for a closed store). At least 39 save sites render the whole route twice, 6 more are mixed. 51 to 66 KB of unchanged shell JSON is re-sent per redraw. 8 progress polls redraw the whole route every 5 to 20 s, hidden tabs included. The notice poll: 4 statements, 60 times an hour per visible tab. 23 to 46 prefetch requests per screen. Source: digest/admin-data.md, m/routes.json.
measures.target_a: Menu: under 2 ms and 110 lookups per build. 0 saves that draw the route twice. Under 30 KB of shell JSON per redraw. No poll ticks in a hidden tab; a progress tick asks its job (2 or 3 statements), not the route; the notice poll asks 2 statements. At most 4 prefetch requests in the 3 s after a screen loads.
measures.how_measured: The count test in src/lib/store-nav.test.ts (AD-1). A scan test with a baseline of client router.refresh() calls (AD-13). The admin.render log line. The request count in e2e/signed-in (CA-5's test). A test that serialises the shell's props (AD-5).
measures.why_this_is_a: One redraw after a save is right; two are not, and a member's 110 menu answers do not change between renders. The floors are one render per save and about 0.1 ms for the memoised menu. 30 KB is what is left when the unread setup area, the closed assistant's words and the menu's repeated addresses go. A B stops at the memo and the double redraws.

measures.name: What makes a cached store page draw again, and what a cold draw costs
measures.today: 71 of 85 cached reads expire after an hour, though 82 carry a tag that every write refreshes. Home and All products redraw every 15 minutes (6 routes). 319 of 1,316 prerendered entries carry the platform-wide tag ai-providers, which any one owner's save refreshes. Every deploy empties every cache (up to 52 deploys on 11 November) and nothing warms it. A cold store page makes an estimated 30 to 35 statements with about 5 waits in a row before its first byte. listPublishedPages() reads 29 whole pages a call: 79,778 calls and 781 s in 78 days, the costliest statement of the app. Source: digest/storefront-data.md, digest/caching.md, m/prod-db-stats.md.
measures.target_a: 0 storefront routes at 15 minutes. A read whose every writer refreshes a tag lives a week; only reads with a clock in them (the 30-day reference price, campaigns, VAT labels) stay hourly. 0 store entries carry a tag that one store's action can refresh for another. A cold store home: 20 statements or fewer and at most 3 waits in a row before the first byte. No caller reads every page to pick one (9 today). After each deploy the job, not a visitor, pays the first draw of Kaizena Flow's home and one store page.
measures.how_measured: scripts/render-modes.mjs baseline (revalidate seconds and tags that name no store, per route). src/server/use-cache.scan.test.ts (every cached read has a life and a tag; no store action refreshes a platform-wide tag). scripts/server-budget.mjs for the first request after a restart. The release job's log of page checks. Production's pg_stat_statements for the whole-pages statement.
measures.why_this_is_a: With tags on 82 of 85 reads the clock adds nothing but redraws: the floor is one draw per change. A deploy still empties every cache, because Next scopes them to a deployment. That cannot be removed, only made cheap (fewer statements, a slimmer cold start) and rarer (the owner's choice on deploys). 20 statements is stricter than the findings' own estimate of 22 to 27, so the cold-draw item must also fold the optional features into one read. A B keeps hourly lives.

measures.name: What a deployment carries per store
measures.today: 4 to 8 routing rules per store with its own domain, against Vercel's cap of 2,048 a deployment, of which the app's own routes take about 705: room for about 270 such stores. One full production deploy per domain change, which empties every cache. The list of store domains is parsed again 2 or 3 times for every link a page draws: at 1,000 stores with a domain about 64 ms per render of a page with 85 links. Source: digest/functions.md (SF-12, SF-13).
measures.target_a: 0 routing rules and 0 deploys per store domain: .next/routes-manifest.json is the same with 0 or 300 active domains. 1 parse of the hosts list per instance. The count of routing rules is printed on every build and shown on Platform, Usage and limits.
measures.how_measured: The new case in src/lib/store-hosts.test.ts (1,000 marketPath() calls parse once). scripts/route-budget.mjs prints the rules in .next/routes-manifest.json. CI's hosts job with a domain activated after the build.
measures.why_this_is_a: Everything else in this area grows with traffic. This grows with the number of stores whether or not anyone visits, and it ends at a wall. The floor is zero per store: a host can be looked up when the request arrives, as the proxy already does for held domains. That replaces decision P8, so it needs the owner's word. Without it the area cannot be an A past a few hundred stores.

work_items.title: Page checks after each deploy: the job, not a visitor, meets the first cold page
work_items.done_when: The release job's log lists the page checks with status 200 after each deploy (Kaizena Flow's home and one page of the template store, from SMOKE_PAGES), and src/lib/await-deploy.test.ts shows that a page answering 500 fails the job.
work_items.moves: Cold draw: the first draw of the named pages after each deploy is paid by the job. No statements saved. Do it first: every lazy-import item below changes the order modules load in, which is how D440 broke a route on Vercel only, and this check is what shows it at deploy. Warming the busy pages of real stores (SD-3 steps 2 and 3) waits until there are visitors to warm for.

tolerated.why: Every one of these reads is cached and tagged, and together they cost about 1.5 s of database time a day. The part that is not cached, the AI provider row read whole 237,563 times, is closed by the slug-and-tiny-facts item and by AI-2. The modal scan over every page's JSON falls with longer cache lives and with the page columns the database area plans. Stated tolerance: a cached, tagged read may fetch a row wider than it shows while the row is under about 10 KB.

About 290 KB and 10 ms per cold instance, and the only cut in the set that could show a shopper the wrong language. Stated tolerance: all four hand-written storefront languages load with a page, 0.4 MB of its 4 MB budget. Look again when a fifth hand-written language is added.

A crawler asks for each store's robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt and feed about once a day, so a one-hour CDN window would save almost nothing. What a cold sitemap costs is what it reads, and the page-list item removes most of that. Add the header when the handlers are next opened.

owner_choices.question: Once stores are open, may a CI run skip its deploy when a newer commit is already on main, so a burst of pushes shares one deploy? Each deploy empties every store's cached pages and starts every function cold (up to 52 deploys on 11 November). It changes D5's 'at once' by a few minutes.

gaps.title: Reads that grow with a store's catalogue, and the cart and checkout, are in no finding
gaps.evidence: The front page reads every active product of the store on each cold draw, to list every product's address in its JSON-LD: src/app/s/[store]/[market]/page.tsx:68 calls listProducts(), which has no limit (src/server/catalog.ts:284-340). A product page's metadata loads the store's whole index, with every product's texts and pictures, to learn one product's markets: p/[handle]/page.tsx:73 and src/server/seo.ts:229. One catalogue tag covers a store, so one price change expires every product page and listing of it (cacheTag(CATALOG_TAG, catalogTag(storeId)) in catalog.ts). The cart reads in a row: eight awaits one after another in cart/cart-contents.tsx:72-198. These are code review steps 3.8, 3.9 and 3.10, all Open (docs/audits/code-review-2026-11.md:110-112). The storefront-data report says they 'are not repeated here', so no step of this plan closes them. The review counted an empty cart only (m/routes.md), and the demo store has 10 products, so none of this shows in any figure. At 2,000 products each cold home page builds 2,000 summaries and each cold product page parses the whole index.
gaps.proposed_work_item: Phase next, effort M. Bring code review steps 3.8 to 3.10 into this plan with numbers. Front page: its JSON-LD from a small cached read of handles, never the summaries. Product metadata: the market codes from getProduct(). Tags: a tag per product on single-product reads and a lists tag, the store's tag kept for store-wide changes. Cart and checkout: the independent reads in one wave. Add a cart with three lines and the checkout to scripts/server-budget.mjs, and seed one test store with 500 products so a read that grows with the catalogue fails a budget. Done when: the budget holds cart and checkout at their counted figures, read in at most two waves after the shopper is known; a cold home page and a cold product page of the 500-product store read no more rows than those of a 10-product store, the listing's own page aside; saving one product refreshes its own tag and the lists tag only.

CI seeds a house store with the switch on, and scripts/render-modes.mjs and scripts/server-budget.mjs hold its home in their baselines. The deploy job's page checks log the cache header and the document's bytes for Kaizena Flow's home. gaps.title: No production figure for a cold start, and the largest fixed cost left after the cuts has no plan
gaps.evidence: Every cold-start number in this area is from the review machine; the draft's section 6 says real cold starts on Vercel were not measured at all. src/instrumentation.ts times nothing, rg finds no cold-start line in src/server/log.ts, docs/capacity.md or docs/performance.md, and the one server budget is the first byte of two warm pages (e2e/performance.spec.ts:127-130). How often instances start cold after opening, with many quiet stores and dozens of deploys a day, is unknown. After every planned cut each function still reads the 10.4 MB server-reference manifest before its first request: 80 to 91 ms and 20 to 24 MB locally, about a third of a lean route's start. SG-16's own done-when stops at 9.4 MB. By its model 547 of the 807 listed routes are admin routes and hold about 62,800 of the entries, because each lists nearly every cached reader, and no step takes them out.
gaps.proposed_work_item: Phase now for the figure, next for the manifest; effort M together. Log one line per instance through log(): instance.start, with the kind of entry, milliseconds from process start to the end of register() and to the first answer, and resident memory; no request data. Show cold starts a day and their p50 and p95 by kind on Platform, Usage and limits, with a target (a beacon within 150 ms of the health check). If the production reading puts the manifest above 30 ms, give the cached readers that 700 or more routes list their own reader files (SG-8's fourth step, first for the readers the admin shell reaches) until the manifest is under 5 MB and 40,000 entries, and report the per-route cost to Next. Done when: the page shows a week of cold-start figures, and the manifest is under 5 MB or shown to cost under 30 ms per cold start in production.
